title: ₹5 Crore Digital Bank Cyberattack: Complete Digital Forensic Investigation
organization: ABC Digital Bank (Scheduled Commercial Banking Entity)
suspectedImpact: ₹5 Crore Unauthorized Outward Transfers & System Ransomware
disclaimer: SIMULATED EDUCATIONAL EVIDENCE: All bank names, accounts, IP addresses, hashes, and financial loss amounts are synthetic training artifacts designed exclusively for SubjectLab forensic education.
objectives: Identify, isolate, and acquire digital evidence across physical endpoints, volatile RAM, smartphones, network taps, and IoT CCTV.
Verify cryptographic SHA-256 hashes and maintain unbroken Chain of Custody documentation conforming to statutory Section 65B requirements.
Examine NTFS storage structures ($MFT), carve deleted customer files from unallocated clusters, and extract Windows execution artifacts (Prefetch, LNK, Registry).
Analyze physical RAM dumps using Volatility 3 (pslist, psscan, netscan, malfind) to uncover hidden rootkits and active C2 connections.
Extract smartphone SQLite databases (SMS OTPs, encrypted messaging) and embedded IoT CCTV firmware to corroborate physical presence.
Construct a normalized UTC Super Timeline, validate forensic tool accuracy against NIST CFTT assertions, and draft a court-admissible forensic report.

evidenceSources.name: Employee Workstation (Dell Latitude 7420)
evidenceSources.evidenceType: Physical NVMe SSD (512 GB) - Bitstream .E01 Image
findings: Prefetch file INVOICE_UPDATE.EXE-B2C4E1A0.pf confirmed 3 executions starting at 08:42:15 UTC.
MFT Record #4812 showed deleted Customer_Accounts.xlsx; carved 18 valid Excel loan spreadsheets from unallocated clusters.
USBSTOR registry entry showed SanDisk USB connected at 14:02:10 UTC (Serial: 4C530001090123115142).
limitations: USB connection artifact proves device was plugged in, but does NOT independently prove files were copied without corroborating shellbag or transfer logs.
Matching image hash confirms bitstream integrity, but does not prove who operated the keyboard.

details.Acquisition Mode: Dead Acquisition via Tableau T8u Write-Blocker

evidenceSources.name: Payment Switch Core Server (HP ProLiant DL380)
evidenceSources.evidenceType: Volatile RAM (64 GB raw dump) & RAID-10 Disk Image (.E01)
findings: Memory triage via Volatility windows.psscan uncovered unlinked rogue process PID 1220 (unknown.exe).
windows.malfind located PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE memory page at 0x7ffe0000 harboring injected MZ shellcode.
windows.netscan revealed PID 1220 holding active TLS socket to 198.51.100.44:443 matching transaction timestamps.
limitations: Process name unknown.exe alone cannot be classified as malware without injected code analysis.
Volatile RAM capture causes minor heisenbug memory footprint modification of ~12 MB.

details.Acquisition Mode: Live Memory Triage (winpmem) followed by static disk imaging

findings: Hardware serial 4C530001090123115142 exactly matches USBSTOR registry entry on Employee Laptop.
File system analysis revealed 0 files in active FAT32 directory; carved 4 system diagnostic scripts from unallocated space.
limitations: No bank customer records were found on this specific USB drive; exfiltration to this drive is uncorroborated.

evidenceSources.name: Employee Smartphone (Samsung Galaxy S23)
evidenceSources.evidenceType: Physical ADB File System Dump (256 GB UFS 4.0)
findings: SMS database mmssms.db-wal showed banking 2FA OTP received at 14:14:22 UTC.
Signal messaging database showed OTP forwarded to unknown recipient at 14:14:45 UTC.
EXIF GPS telemetry placed device in server room vicinity (18.9220 N, 72.8347 E) at 14:10:00 UTC.
limitations: Biometric fingerprint unlock artifact proves phone was unlocked, but cannot verify whether employee was coerced.

evidenceSources.name: Core Firewall & Perimeter Network Taps
evidenceSources.source: Cisco ASA 5585-X & Internal Core Switch SPAN Port
evidenceSources.evidenceType: Full PCAP (14.2 GB) & IPFIX / NetFlow Database
findings: 1,420 outbound TLS sessions established between server 10.14.10.12 and external IP 198.51.100.44:443.
60-second periodic intervals with 5% jitter, consistent with Cobalt Strike beacon configuration.
High-volume encrypted burst (42 MB) observed immediately prior to transaction execution.
limitations: NetFlow records lack application payloads; TLS payload decryption required private key recovery from RAM.

evidenceSources.name: AWS Cloud & API Gateway Audit Logs
evidenceSources.source: CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs & Amazon EKS Audit Stream
findings: API Gateway logged 14 unauthorized RTGS fund transfer calls originating from payment switch internal IP.
Total transfer sum calculated: ₹5,00,00,000 across 14 beneficiary accounts within 6 minutes.
limitations: CloudTrail records confirm API key was used; they cannot verify whether the key was stolen or authorized.

evidenceSources.name: Smart CCTV & Physical Access Badge Records
evidenceSources.source: Hikvision IP Camera & Server Room RFID Access Controller
evidenceSources.evidenceType: Embedded Flash Dump (MicroSD ring buffer) & SQL Access Log
findings: RFID badge log shows Employee Badge #402 swiped at server room door at 14:09:42 UTC.
Recovered CCTV video frame confirms employee physically entered server vault at 14:10:00 UTC.
limitations: CCTV camera internal clock was drifting by +3 minutes 12 seconds; normalized to NTP reference.

stages.title: Stage 1: Evidence Identification & Preservation
stages.subtitle: Foundations, Legal Compliance & Write-Blocked Imaging
stages.objective: Identify evidence sources, apply RFC 3227 order of volatility, attach write-blockers, compute baseline SHA-256 hashes, and log Chain of Custody entries.

activities.title: Order of Volatility Triage
activities.instruction: Select the correct immediate action when arriving at the live payment switch server (Item E-02).
activities.prompt: The payment switch server is currently active and beaconing to an external IP. What should the first responder execute first?

options.label: Immediately pull the power cord to prevent further fund transfers
options.feedback: INCORRECT: Pulling the power cord destroys physical RAM, wiping active processes, encryption keys, and C2 sockets permanently.

options.label: Capture physical RAM via winpmem before disconnecting network or powering off
options.feedback: CORRECT: Conforms to RFC 3227 order of volatility, capturing volatile in-memory malware and sockets before severance.

options.label: Reboot into Safe Mode and run Windows Defender
options.feedback: INCORRECT: Rebooting destroys volatile memory and contaminates file system timestamps.

activities.explanation: RFC 3227 establishes that physical RAM is highly volatile and must be secured before non-volatile storage or rebooting.

activities.title: Hardware Write-Blocker Verification
activities.instruction: Evaluate the forensic necessity of a hardware write-blocker during acquisition of the employee laptop (Item E-01).
activities.prompt: Why must the analyst connect a hardware write-blocker between the suspect drive and the forensic workstation?

options.label: To increase the read and write transfer speed of the SATA bus
options.feedback: Incorrect: Write-blockers protect data integrity, not bus speed.

options.label: To intercept and drop SCSI/ATA write commands, guaranteeing the source disk cannot be modified
options.feedback: Correct: Prevents host OS mounting or auto-writing to evidence media.

options.label: To automatically decrypt BitLocker partitions without a password
options.feedback: Incorrect: Write-blockers do not perform cryptographic decryption.

activities.explanation: A write-blocker physically intercepts write signals, ensuring the master evidence media remains pristine.

stages.title: Stage 2: File System Recovery & Artifact Examination
stages.subtitle: NTFS Structures, Carving & Windows Execution Footprints
stages.objective: Inspect the employee laptop's NTFS $MFT, carve deleted Excel loan documents from unallocated space, and analyze Prefetch, LNK, and Registry artifacts.

activities.title: Windows Prefetch (.pf) Analysis
activities.instruction: Interpret the prefetch artifact found on the employee's workstation: INVOICE_UPDATE.EXE-B2C4E1A0.pf.
activities.prompt: What does the existence of this Prefetch file with execution count = 3 conclusively prove?

options.label: It proves the employee intentionally stole ₹5 crore
options.feedback: INCORRECT: Prefetch proves application execution, not legal intent or financial theft.

options.label: It proves invoice_update.exe was executed on this machine 3 times
options.feedback: CORRECT: Windows Prefetch records program execution counts, timestamps, and loaded DLLs.

options.label: It proves invoice_update.exe is certified clean by Microsoft
options.feedback: INCORRECT: Prefetch records execution regardless of whether the binary is benign or malicious.

activities.explanation: Prefetch files prove application execution on a Windows endpoint, but do not establish the subjective intent of the user.

activities.title: Deleted File Carving
activities.instruction: Identify the magic byte header and footer required to carve the deleted customer loan file (PDF/XLSX).
activities.prompt: Which hex signature identifies the start of an OpenXML document (e.g. Customer_Accounts.xlsx)?

options.label: FF D8 FF E0 (JPEG)
options.feedback: Incorrect: This is JPEG format.

options.label: 50 4B 03 04 (PK.. ZIP Header)
options.feedback: Correct: Microsoft XLSX/DOCX are ZIP containers starting with PK.. (0x504B0304).

options.label: 25 50 44 46 (%PDF)
options.feedback: Incorrect: This is Adobe PDF format.

activities.explanation: Modern Office OpenXML files (.xlsx, .docx) are structured ZIP packages marked by the PK.. magic header.

stages.title: Stage 3: Memory Triage & Network Reconstruction
stages.subtitle: Volatility Framework, Rootkits & Super Timeline Synthesis
stages.objective: Execute Volatility plugins on switch memory dump, isolate unlinked PID 1220 unknown.exe, correlate NetFlow C2 beacons, and build a normalized UTC timeline.

activities.title: Volatility Process Scanning
activities.instruction: Analyze the output of Volatility plugins on switch_memory.raw.
activities.prompt: windows.pslist showed no unknown processes, but windows.psscan revealed PID 1220 unknown.exe. What technique did the adversary use?

options.label: Direct Kernel Object Manipulation (DKOM) to unlink the process from ActiveProcessLinks
options.feedback: CORRECT: DKOM unlinks processes from the standard doubly-linked list, hiding them from pslist while psscan detects pool tags.

options.label: Overwriting the MBR partition table
options.feedback: INCORRECT: MBR manipulation affects disk bootloaders, not live in-memory process lists.

options.label: Formatting the primary NTFS volume
options.feedback: INCORRECT: The server was running actively.

activities.explanation: DKOM rootkits modify kernel structures to hide processes from standard enumeration APIs, but memory pool scanners locate them.

activities.title: C2 Network Beaconing Identification
activities.instruction: Evaluate the firewall PCAP log displaying periodic connections to 198.51.100.44:443.
activities.prompt: Why is 60-second periodic outbound traffic with 5% jitter characteristic of advanced malware command-and-control?

options.label: It represents standard Windows NTP clock synchronization
options.feedback: Incorrect: NTP operates via UDP port 123 at much longer intervals.

options.label: Adversary implants use randomized sleep intervals (jitter) to blend into regular traffic and evade threshold alarms
options.feedback: Correct: Jitter prevents simple static periodicity detection while maintaining regular heartbeat checks.

options.label: It proves the employee was streaming YouTube videos
options.feedback: Incorrect: Video streaming uses continuous high-throughput media connections.

activities.explanation: Adversary implants add jitter (random variance) to prevent deterministic beaconing alerts.

stages.title: Stage 4: Specialized Device & IoT Investigation
stages.subtitle: Mobile Extraction, SQLite Parsing & CCTV Correlation
stages.objective: Acquire employee smartphone file system, parse SQLite WAL logs for SMS OTPs and Signal chats, extract IoT CCTV firmware, and correlate physical presence.

activities.title: SQLite WAL Journal Analysis
activities.instruction: Examine the extracted mmssms.db-wal file from the employee's smartphone.
activities.prompt: The primary database mmssms.db did not show the incoming bank OTP, but mmssms.db-wal contained the OTP received at 14:14:22 UTC. Why?

options.label: The Write-Ahead Log holds recent transactions that have not yet been checkpointed into the master database
options.feedback: CORRECT: In SQLite WAL mode, uncommitted or recently committed transactions remain in the WAL file until a checkpoint.

options.label: The employee deleted the entire operating system
options.feedback: INCORRECT: The device was fully operational.

options.label: The WAL file is an encrypted BitLocker volume
options.feedback: INCORRECT: WAL is a standard SQLite logging journal.

activities.explanation: SQLite databases write changes first to the WAL companion journal, preserving recent and deleted records before consolidation.

activities.title: Physical Presence vs Digital Action
activities.instruction: Correlate the IoT CCTV footage with the server room access log at 14:10:00 UTC.
activities.prompt: Does the CCTV recording of the employee entering the server room prove they typed the transaction command?

options.label: Yes, entering the room conclusively proves they authorized the transfer
options.feedback: Incorrect: Presence in a room does not prove physical keystrokes on a specific server console.

options.label: No, it corroborates physical opportunity, but terminal keystroke or session logs are required to prove action
options.feedback: Correct: Forensic distinction between physical opportunity and direct attribution.

options.label: No, because CCTV footage is legally inadmissible in all courts
options.feedback: Incorrect: CCTV footage is admissible under electronic evidence rules when certified.

activities.explanation: Physical presence confirms opportunity and location, but requires digital terminal logs to substantiate action.

stages.title: Stage 5: Final Validation & Forensic Report
stages.subtitle: NIST CFTT Verification, Defensible Reporting & Courtroom Testimony
stages.objective: Verify tool reliability against NIST CFTT assertions, review the Master Evidence Register, simulate expert witness cross-examination, and author the court report.

activities.title: Expert Witness Cross-Examination Defense
activities.instruction: Answer defense counsel's challenge regarding the seized SanDisk USB drive (Item E-04).
activities.prompt: Counsel: 'Inspector, you found my client's USB drive plugged into the laptop. Doesn't that prove they stole the customer accounts?' How do you answer?

options.label: 'Yes, the presence of the USB drive in the registry confirms the theft.'
options.feedback: INCORRECT: This is speculative advocacy. USBSTOR proves connection, not file exfiltration.

options.label: 'The registry proves the USB drive was mounted at 14:02 UTC. However, no file transfer logs or shellbag entries confirm data was copied to that drive.'
options.feedback: CORRECT: Demonstrates strict forensic objectivity, separating confirmed observations from unsupported leaps.

options.label: 'I refuse to answer because that is confidential police work.'
options.feedback: INCORRECT: Expert witnesses must answer transparently under cross-examination.

activities.explanation: Objective expert testimony avoids the advocacy trap and states precise evidentiary boundaries.

activities.title: NIST CFTT Tool Validation Check
activities.instruction: Confirm tool qualification under the Daubert evidentiary standard.
activities.prompt: Why does citing NIST Computer Forensic Tool Testing (CFTT) test reports strengthen report admissibility in court?

options.label: It satisfies the Daubert requirement for peer-reviewed, empirically tested tools with known error rates
options.feedback: Correct: NIST CFTT provides empirical benchmarking verifying forensic tools meet rigorous test assertions.

options.label: It grants diplomatic immunity to the investigating team
options.feedback: Incorrect: CFTT is a technical benchmark, not a legal immunity treaty.

options.label: It eliminates the need to provide evidence hashes
options.feedback: Incorrect: Hashes are always mandatory.

activities.explanation: NIST CFTT reports establish known error rates and empirical reliability required under Daubert and statutory standards.
